clue.text: They shared troughs, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of shared troughs are one possible arrangement among others to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene: animals who ate side by side at the same water troughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes an anagram of SHARED TROUGHS; the whole clue is also the definition, since working horses did share troughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy farm horses were watered together at communal troughs, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Shabby Italian rider's content to go up bridle path

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, a reversal

parts.note: shabby clothes are worn

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: Frankie Dettori is the Italian-born champion jockey

explanation.surface: A down-at-heel Italian horseman happy to ride up a riding track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' trims DETTORI to ETTOR; WORN + ETTOR read upwards ('to go up') gives the answer. ROTTEN ROW is the horse-riding track in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten Row is a famous track in Hyde Park laid out for riding horses, a named example of a bridleway.

clue.text: Range of paintings defaced

indicators.note: defaced here means the face, or front letter, is taken off the word

parts.note: murals are paintings done on walls

explanation.surface: A collection of artworks that have been vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like part of a description of the art, but it is the definition; 'defaced' drops the M of MURALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are a mountain range dividing Europe from Asia, and range is a word for a chain of mountains.

clue.text: Attentive husband occasionally found out — slippery character to catch!

indicators.note: the eel catching something means it holds those letters within it

parts.note: an eel is the proverbially slippery creature

indicators.note: out here means the chosen letters are put out of order, to be rearranged
occasionally means only some letters of found are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: A husband pays close attention while an evasive figure is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' and 'out' work in sequence: alternate letters of 'found' are taken, then scrambled before the slippery character catches them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be heedful is to pay heed, taking careful notice, which is what being attentive means.

clue.text: Entertaining woman in stockings — time to get extremely suspicious

indicators.note: the stockings get, or take in, the extra letter, so it goes inside them

parts.note: hose is an old collective word for stockings

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, the first and last, of suspicious

explanation.surface: A woman in stockings, and it's time someone grew very suspicious of her.
explanation.walkthrough: HOSE takes in T ('to get'), then 'extremely' gives SS, the outside letters of suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess is a woman who entertains guests at her home.

clue.text: Sun's nice and relaxing — but could this presage a change?

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, and the 's stands for has

indicators.note: relaxing suggests letters loosened and shaken out of order

explanation.surface: Lovely sunshine and easy living, yet something hints the weather may turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' rearranges NICE AND after RA. The change foreseen is a change in the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain dance is a ritual performed to bring rainfall, so it would foretell a change from sunny weather.

clue.text: Not a reason to give up — an inspiration

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
the words Not a reason give up, or yield, letters held within them

explanation.surface: An argument against quitting, framed as a source of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' takes OTARE from inside 'nOT A REason' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek Muse of lyric poetry, and a muse is a source of inspiration to artists.

clue.text: When running helps at a fight

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are in motion, moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a brawl, but only while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' looks like part of the story but is the definition: a time answers the question when. 'running' rearranges HELPS AT A FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Half past eight is a clock time, an answer to the question of when something happens.

clue.text: Train fare?

parts.note: reads as the price of a rail ticket, but fare is food, and a train runs on wheels, so food delivered on wheels

explanation.surface: The cost of a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare means food as well as a ticket price; this food service comes by vehicle rather than by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals on wheels is a service that delivers cooked food by van to elderly or housebound people.

clue.text: Army personnel will feed them

parts.note: reads as soldiers serving food, but army ants are insects that some creatures eat

explanation.surface: Soldiers will provide meals for some group.
explanation.walkthrough: The army here is army ants, which travel in vast columns; the personnel are eaten, not cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Anteaters are mammals that live on ants and termites, so army ants would be their food.

clue.text: Correctly positioned on motorway when lorry at the front pulled out — ridiculous!

indicators.note: a lorry pulling out leaves its lane, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: a car properly placed on a multi-lane road is in lane

indicators.note: at the front means the first letter of lorry

explanation.surface: A driver fumes at a lorry swinging out ahead on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' gives L, the first letter of lorry, and 'pulled out' removes it from IN LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, a close synonym of ridiculous.

clue.text: Lets out cry: 'Don't move a muscle!'

indicators.note: a cry is something spoken out, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: the command freeze means stay completely still

explanation.surface: Someone releases a prisoner while shouting at them to stay still.
explanation.walkthrough: The shouted order 'Freeze!' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone is to let them out, of prison or captivity.

clue.text: Accepting work, easily filled a basket

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is held inside the other
easily suggests the letters of filled a fall loosely into another order

parts.note: go means work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone took on a job and had a basket filled with no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily' rearranges FILLED A into FIELDAL, which takes in GO ('Accepting').
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball, a basket scored during open play is called a field goal.

clue.text: A challenge keeping close to Jennifer and Dawn

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the letter is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: to rival someone is to challenge them

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of Jennifer

explanation.surface: Two women, Jennifer and Dawn, locked in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' reads as a woman's name but is the definition; 'close to' gives R, which A RIVAL is 'keeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the arrival of day, as in the dawn of a new era.

clue.text: One confirming truth about Scotland's number one poet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the letter

parts.note: a verifier is someone who confirms that something is true

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of Scotland's

explanation.surface: Someone checks facts about Scotland's greatest poet, presumably Burns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland's number one' suggests Burns, but gives only S, which VERIFIER goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A versifier is someone who writes verse, a poet, often a minor one.

clue.text: Round back of house, see mostly older type of plant

indicators.note: round means going around, so the trimmed word encloses the other letters
mostly means most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: senior means older

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of house

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced the same as see

explanation.surface: A gardener directs a visitor round the back of the house to see an old plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SENIOR to SENIO, which goes 'Round' E (from 'back of house') and C. The see here is the letter name, not a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: Senecio is a large genus of flowering plants, including ragworts and groundsels.

clue.text: Auctioneer carelessly spilling sweetheart's drink

indicators.note: carelessly means the letters are rearranged, and spilling means one of them is lost along the way

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A clumsy auctioneer knocks over his sweetheart's glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly spilling' rearranges AUCTIONEER after one E is lost; the E is the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Crosses town to get suit, changing direction once

parts.note: T is given as an abbreviation for town, as on maps

indicators.note: one compass direction is swapped for another, a single time: east becomes west

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits of playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone heads into town for a suit, but turns about on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing direction once' swaps HEARTS' E (east) for W (west).
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone is to oppose or frustrate their plans, which is what thwarting means.

clue.text: Showing signs of damage in chicken run

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the other word

parts.note: chicken means cowardly, scared
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A chicken run that has been knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken run' reads as a hen enclosure; split it to put R in SCARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarred bears marks left by injury or harm.

clue.text: Seat about six inside trailer

indicators.note: inside means these pieces are put within the other word

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in church
re means about or concerning
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A seat with a capacity of about six fitted in a towed vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' reads as a towed vehicle; it means a film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer gives a preview of a film, a short glimpse shown in advance.

clue.text: Totally clean? Not you, no way, Mr Johnson

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so the letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: pure means completely clean, unmixed
U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters for way are taken out

parts.note: Mr is short for mister
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A sarcastic retort: is Mr Johnson spotless? Certainly not you.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was UK Prime Minister when this appeared. Mr does double duty: it is part of the scene and gives MISTER, which loses ST ('no way').
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was then Britain's prime minister, and premier is another title for a head of government.

clue.text: Naughty boy — story about Tom maybe giving finger

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: about means going round, so the story surrounds the cat

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
a tom is a male cat, so tom is an example of cat

explanation.surface: A mischievous boy tells tales about someone called Tom, pointing the finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finger' is the verb: to finger someone is to name them as guilty. 'Tom' reads as a person but is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is slang for accusing them, and implicating means showing them to be involved in a crime.

clue.text: Small bottle, as originally described by Collins?

indicators.note: described means drawn round, so the name is drawn around the letter

parts.note: Phil Collins is the English drummer and singer of Genesis

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of as

explanation.surface: A little bottle as one Collins once portrayed it, perhaps in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collins' suggests the dictionary or Wilkie Collins; it is Phil Collins.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, especially one for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Lowry's first painting lacking substance? What about Turner?

indicators.note: first means the first letter of Lowry's
the substance of a short word is its middle, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: painting is art

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: eh? is a way of asking what?

explanation.surface: An art critic says Lowry's work is thin compared with Turner's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowry' and 'Turner' are both painters in the surface, but Turner is the definition: a machine that turns. 'lacking substance' removes the middle letter; 'about' reverses the word for what.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe turns a workpiece to shape it, so it is literally a machine that turns.

clue.text: Wind-up? Why to be wary

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to reel in a line is to wind it
the letter Y is pronounced the same as why

explanation.surface: Someone being teased asks why they should be suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind-up' reads as a tease; split, 'Wind' is REEL and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means suspicious or cautious, a near-synonym of wary.

clue.text: Henry has two islands and part of another

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an ait is a small river island, and I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A man called Henry owns a couple of islands and a share of a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' reads as a man; it is the physics unit. AIT is an islet in a river, notably on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti occupies the western part of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: What will Jack do? That bloke's going to cause trouble!

parts.note: a car jack raises the vehicle off the ground
he'll is short for he will, that man is going to

explanation.surface: Wondering what Jack will do next, someone warns that man is about to make a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a man; it is the lifting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for making an uproar or causing serious trouble.

clue.text: Historical victim of prejudice, right? Lady suffered terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman suffered dreadfully from bigotry in history, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges R with LADY SUFFERED. Dreyfus was a French Jewish army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Dreyfus was falsely convicted amid antisemitism, making him a historical figure wronged by prejudice.
